Last Saturday was my first Devils hockey game, and they won 4–1.

Dear Reader,

Here’s what I learned from attending a professional hockey game:
	•	There are three periods, each 20 minutes long. In between periods, there’s an 18-minute break—just enough time to question your life choices and buy overpriced snacks.

	•	Players change constantly or get benched because they do an alarming number of power moves, sprints, and full-body slams. (This is great for fitness junkies.)

	•	The crowd is basically a mega-church gathering: ma, pa, kids, babies, grandparents—everyone comes to worship the puck.

	•	Every time the Devils score, the crowd lovingly chants, “You suck!” Sportsmanship is alive and well.

	•	“C’mon! It’s not tennis!” yelled one particularly passionate (read: drunk) fan from behind me.

	•	“Look, Ma! I made it on TV!” screamed another drunken fan when his face appeared on the gigantic stadium screen/jumbotron. Dreams really do come true.

	•	Some kind of dramatic French horn blasts when there are a few minutes left on the clock, signaling something important that I did not fully understand.

So yes, that’s what I learned from my first hockey game in a long time. ;)

Anyway, thank you again to my date for inviting me, paying for my ticket and water bottle, and occasionally translating what was happening on the ice. 😉

Do you like live sports games? Have a nice one. ^^

~ Susanna

Pude cumplir sueños y metas que antes solo existían en mi imaginación y en mi mente soñadora.

Como mensaje final quiero decirte esto: la vida es bonita. No dejes de creer en el amor. Vive lleno/a de esperanza y aprende; de todo lo que te pase, aprende. Sé bueno/a contigo, no te castigues, elige vivir el presente y, si en algún momento no puedes, aférrate a las promesas de Dios y busca apoyo profesional. Te abrazo. Eres importante.

Welcome to the enchanting world of our Pizzaiolo, a true artisan with a heartfelt passion for every batch of pizza dough! With every knead, twist, and toss, he transforms simple ingredients into mouthwatering masterpieces—a delicate dance of culinary artistry.

And then comes that exhilarating moment of tossing the dough high into the air, a breathtaking skill cultivated through years of dedication. Watching it spin gracefully is not just a technique; it’s a joyful celebration that enchants everyone around, connecting our tradition with every twirl. 

Behind each slice of our authentic Neapolitan pizza lies a journey filled with moments of joy, laughter, and passion. Join us at La Sorrentina, where we elevate the humble pizza into a heartfelt experience—every bite tells the story of love from our Pizzaiolo’s hands to your plate.

The Supper Club December review... Bareli's in Secaucus .  A nice cozy little Italian place. There is something about this place--it has good bones as my mom would say, and the food is very good. For appetizers we ordered THREE ORDERS OF MEATBALLS--yes they were that good. Off the hook!  A Supper Club first.  Other apps that were good:  shrimp cocktail, angry spring rolls and sausage and peppers. All very good.  The only complaint was that the appetizers were small and not really shareable. 

We all shared the black spaghetti with shrimp as a mini entree. Was very very good. 

For the main course:  Skinny John got the Swordfish special, which was very good.  Gabe had the double cut pork chop--a signature of the place--it was AMAZING.  I had the 18oz Veal Chop, in a mushroom demi glaze.  The entrees were OUTSTANDING!! 

For dessert we had the ricotta cheesecake, the tartufo, and the biscotti.  All were solid. 

Overall a solid place. 3.9 Forks.

Introduction to Gelli Printing 12/11 @6.30
Gelli printing is a fun mono printing technique that uses a soft, reusable gel plate to create unique, textured prints on paper, without a traditional press.  We use various tools, stencils and natural objects to create textures and patterns before pressing paper onto the plate to transfer the design. This is a workshop of experimenting with colors and structures. The results are vibrant, beautiful and always surprising. $5 off pp for group of 4 and up BYOB Tea and cookies included.

Hey yall happy Sunday!!! Back with a little Jersey review since I’m home this weekend🏡❤️. Last night, myself, @kellyingenito & my dad headed over to one of their favorite restaurants, the Saddle River Inn. Historically, I’ve never been the biggest fan of the food, but I appreciate the ambiance. However, I had the best meal I’ve ever had there last night, so I figured it deserved a review! Unfortunately for me as a non-wine drinker, Saddle River Inn is BYOB, so I had a #sober dinner, but enjoyed a crisp Coke 🥤💋. For appetizers, we shared two of their new menu items which were both truffle-centric and both delicious as hell: the Truffle Grilled Cheese and the Truffle Agnolotti. The grilled cheese came out first and was soooo delishy. The truffle was just enough without being overpowering, and the cheese was melty and yummy. The only thing is it needed to be eaten right away while it’s hot, because it got cold fairly quickly. The agnolotti came out next and they so kindly split them into portions of two for each of us— these were also fabulous. Silky smooth filling and a rich truffley sauce❤️ mmmm. I also enjoyed their crabmeat salad, which has been on the menu but was new to me, and came with cabbage, pickled pear, and a sesame dressing. The crab was fresh and plentiful, and all of the flavors went really well together. For my main, I had the special Halibut which came over spaghetti squash with some fried garlic on top. This was sooooo good. The halibut was buttery soft and seasoned well, and it went really well with the spaghetti squash. It was a funky pairing that I never would have thought of, but it was truly delectable and probably my favorite bite of the night. My mom also enjoyed their lobster roll as her entree which came on a pretzel bun and was topped with caviar— totally up her alley (and mine 🤣). All in all, the service here is impeccable, the ambiance is cozy and special, and the food (especially with the new menu) is great, even if I haven’t always liked it 😊💋👩‍🍳 #nj #njeats #eats #food #foodie #saddleriverinn #newjersey #jerseygirl #dinner

Hey everyone, let me tell you my story—so far.

I spent eight and a half years as a United States Marine. That life shaped me in ways I’ll never fully explain: the discipline, the brotherhood, the missions, the nights you don’t talk about, and the mornings you’re just grateful to see. I gave everything I had to the Corps, and it gave me everything I needed to become the man I am today. On October 20, 2025, I walked away from active duty with my head high, knowing I’d served with honor.
Civilian life hit fast. Almost right away, I landed a job as a Federal Background Investigator—digging into people’s lives, making sure the right ones got clearance. It was intense, detail-heavy work that used a lot of the skills the Marine Corps drilled into me. But something bigger was waiting.
That’s when I met her—my fiancée. From the first moment, it just felt right. She saw all of me: the Marine, the quiet parts, the loud parts, the parts still figuring things out. And I saw my future in her eyes.
On October 1, 2025, I made one of the biggest decisions of my life: I quit the investigator job, packed everything I owned, and moved to New Jersey to be with her. No plan B, no regrets—just a leap because love like this doesn’t come around twice.
We settled into life together quickly. Late November rolled around, and we looked at each other and said, “Why not go all in on what we really want?” So we did. We decided to chase content creation full time. No more clocking in for someone else’s mission—we’re building our own now. Every ride on my Harley, every bridge I cross from New York to Jersey, every Starbucks run I make for her, every mile we put on the odometer… it’s all part of the story we’re telling the world.
I’ve lived a few lives already: warrior, investigator, rider, partner, creator. I’ve traded dress blues for leather, security badges for camera gear, and orders for freedom. And honestly? I’ve never felt more alive.
This is just the beginning. The road’s wide open, she’s right beside me, and we’re writing the next chapters together—one post, one ride, one fearless choice at a time.
Thanks for coming along on this journey with us. Stick around… the best is yet to come.
